dataset_meta.dataset_name: EatOuts Designer Marketplace — Five Designer Demo Seed
dataset_meta.created_for: Local visual demonstration and end-to-end UI testing of EatOuts designer services, business briefs, designer workspace, admin operations, retainers and payouts.
dataset_meta.seed_strategy: Idempotent merge/upsert by stable id; preserve existing user data and existing keys; do not clear localStorage or overwrite non-demo records.
dataset_meta.recommended_demo_switch: Enable only in the existing app demo/development mode; never insert this dataset into production by default.
dataset_meta.service_catalog_authority: eatouts-services-seed.js / existing shared service catalogue is authoritative. Convert service_reference_keys by matching actual service identifiers when integrating; do not create a competing catalogue based on this file.
dataset_meta.workflow_authority: eatouts-brand-kit.js (or the actual shared marketplace module) is authoritative for pricing, commission, reservations, capacity, statuses, migration and audit events.

beverage-promos.purpose: Beverage promotion artwork, drink launches, cooler campaigns and product promo graphics

alcohol-promos.purpose: Alcohol-brand promotions, lounge/nightlife campaigns, bottle features and responsible event promotions

events.purpose: Event flyers, party campaigns, live music posters, brunches, markets and countdown artwork

asset_linking_requirements.assignment_policy: Use distinct existing files if available; link each selected image to exactly one portfolio item and one designer record unless the existing system explicitly supports shared ownership.
asset_linking_requirements.if_count_is_short: Do not duplicate files silently or claim the requirement passed. Report the exact count and shortage for that folder, and leave unresolved slots visibly marked in the manifest.
asset_linking_requirements.if_files_are_not_supported_images: Report skipped files with reasons; do not link corrupt or non-image files.
asset_linking_requirements.if_title_does_not_match_artwork: Retitle or rewrite the fictional portfolio caption based on the actual image, and keep all client/product/event facts labelled as unverified demo content.

designers.tagline: Bold promo design for places people want to be.
designers.bio: KudiGotDis Creative builds punchy, easy-to-read promotional design for bars, beverage brands, restaurants, DJs and event organisers. The studio leans into strong hierarchy, energetic colour, large headlines and mobile-first layouts that stay legible in WhatsApp shares and Instagram stories. This is fictional demonstration copy; replace it with the real designer biography before production.
designers.long_bio: The fictional KudiGotDis demo profile represents a versatile independent designer who understands the practical pressure behind small-business promotions: a clear offer, a recognisable product, a date and venue that can be read quickly, and a design that looks intentional even when viewed on a small phone. The portfolio examples are demo case studies mapped to image slots from the app’s local asset folders; they must not be presented as verified commercial client work.

working_preferences.deliverables: PNG/JPG previews; editable/source files only when included in the agreed scope
working_preferences.communication: In-app job thread first; configured EatOuts admin handoff for escalations

capacity_demo.capacity_note: One active one-time job is shown as in progress in the demo. Pending admin approval is not counted as an approved active slot.

designers.pricing_notes: Catalogue pricing is governed by the shared EatOuts service seed, not by this profile. The prices inside demo jobs are immutable example snapshots only.

demo_private_profile.payout_method: Unconfigured demo payout; no bank or wallet details stored

designers.tagline: Clean layouts, confident brands and menus that sell.
designers.bio: NeoFrame Studio specialises in structured brand systems, restaurant menus, beverage product tiles and practical layouts for print and digital use. The studio favours consistent spacing, restrained colour, clear pricing and reusable templates that a small business can keep using after a campaign ends. This is fictional demo copy, not a verified biography.
designers.long_bio: The fictional NeoFrame profile represents a methodical designer for businesses that want a coherent visual system rather than a one-off graphic. Example work ranges from a readable food menu to clean product-led beverage creative and event artwork with strong information hierarchy. Portfolio image associations must be verified against the actual local files before they are displayed as finished examples.

working_preferences.feedback: One decision-maker and one consolidated revision list
working_preferences.deliverables: Screen-ready preview plus print-ready export where included

designers.bio: Thuto Motion Lab focuses on animated promo assets, event countdowns, teaser concepts and high-energy key art that can be adapted across short-form social channels. Static portfolio images are used here as poster/key-art examples; actual motion previews should only appear when a matching video file exists. Fictional demo profile.
designers.long_bio: This sample profile demonstrates how a motion-focused designer can still display static poster frames in the portfolio while offering motion design as a separately priced service. The app should never pretend a JPG is a playable video. Where only a still image exists, label it as artwork or preview frame and show a motion-play indicator only if a valid video asset is linked.

working_preferences.feedback: Timing/text changes collected before final export
working_preferences.deliverables: Preview MP4/GIF only where motion deliverables are explicitly included

designers.tagline: Artwork built to work on screen and in print.
designers.bio: Mpho Printworks handles business cards, table tents, shopfront graphics, takeaway packaging and practical retail artwork. The profile highlights print preparation, legibility, trim/bleed awareness and designs that can carry a brand across physical touchpoints. Fictional demo profile.
designers.long_bio: This demo designer is intended to let an admin test briefs that require physical production details, dimensions, stock or substrate notes, and a clear distinction between design fees and printer/manufacturer costs. The EatOuts design fee must not be presented as including third-party printing unless the accepted quote says so.

working_preferences.briefing: Final dimensions, printer specs, logos and exact contact/pricing text
working_preferences.feedback: Proof approval required before final print export
working_preferences.deliverables: Print-ready PDF only when requested and in scope; preview PNG for approval

designers.tagline: A month of consistent content, not a pile of random posts.
designers.bio: Dineo Social Studio builds coordinated social content for small hospitality businesses, beverage brands and event organisers. Work is planned around a campaign message, repeatable templates, offer clarity and a consistent posting rhythm. Monthly retainers should show exact deliverable quantities, due dates, revision limits and approval expectations. Fictional demo profile.
designers.long_bio: This sample profile is useful for testing the difference between a one-time pack and a continuing retainer. Its demo scenarios include an active social-content project and a retainer flagged for payment attention. A missed-payment warning should alert the administrator for review; the application must not silently cancel or release capacity just because a demo counter says a cycle is overdue.

working_preferences.briefing: Monthly offer calendar, event dates, product photos, prices and approved brand assets
working_preferences.feedback: Business approves each scheduled batch before publishing
working_preferences.deliverables: Design files and a content schedule; publishing/community management excluded unless contracted

demo_test_scenarios.title: Business browses designers and samples
demo_test_scenarios.expected: Service page shows at least five cards, category filters, working portfolio thumbnails and a visible demo label; private email/phone and payout fields remain hidden.

demo_test_scenarios.title: Business submits single promo brief
demo_test_scenarios.expected: Selection -> brief -> price summary -> submission; pricing freezes at submit; job enters pending admin approval; tentative reservation is visible but does not increment approved active capacity until admin approval.

demo_test_scenarios.title: Admin reviews and approves job
demo_test_scenarios.expected: Admin action records actor/timestamp in audit; reservation is checked centrally; capacity count updates only after approval; reject/hold options exist if capacity is full.

demo_test_scenarios.title: Designer submits draft and client requests revision
demo_test_scenarios.expected: Designer can update their own assigned job only; client can request revision; revision rounds and status history remain visible.

demo_test_scenarios.title: Client accepts; admin closes job and marks payout
demo_test_scenarios.expected: Client satisfaction alone does not release capacity; admin closes job, capacity is released once, payout status moves through the supported admin-controlled states, and commission/payout arithmetic matches frozen quote.

demo_test_scenarios.title: Retainer cycle and overdue payment
demo_test_scenarios.expected: Show monthly scope, deliverable quantity, due dates, revision limits, and cycle history; two missed cycles flag admin review and do not silently cancel the retainer or release capacity.

demo_test_scenarios.title: No client activity for 14 days

seed_safety_notes: All names, reviews, client organizations, ratings, metrics, dates and transaction states in this file are fabricated demo data.
The KudiGotDis record uses an invented .example.test email and no real phone or payout coordinates.
Demo payout records must never trigger a real payment, transfer, invoice, message or WhatsApp handoff.
Do not expose private designer profile fields to business users. Keep role checks in shared auth/data logic, not merely in the UI.
If the app already has a demo seed or a canonical job store, adapt this dataset through the existing model instead of creating a second competing storage system.
